You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: 🔥 Bitget US Stock Hot-Spot Strike｜2026.09.23  Main theme: Memory chips surge across the board｜Agentic AI · Physical robotics · Trump–Xi summit · Quantum

TEXT:
1. Memory chips repriced as AI infrastructure
Micron rose 5% and SanDisk nearly 7%, with Seagate and Western Digital moving in tandem; the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index logged a sixth straight gain. Rosenblatt initiated coverage on SNDK at Buy with a $2,400 target, recasting NAND from commodity storage into a system-critical AI component. SanDisk’s datacenter revenue jumped from $960 million in FY25 to $5.15 billion in FY26. Micron reports after the close on September 30, putting the HBM/memory supply-demand story into a verification window.
🎯 Beneficiaries: MU , SNDK, STX , WDC ; Key catalyst: Analyst repricing plus pre-earnings flows crowding into memory.
2. Meta Muse turns agents from concept into traffic
Muse has topped the US App Store free chart and can send emails, compare prices, and place orders. After META jumped more than 11% on Monday, the chip complex kept a premium while consumer software was re-rated: Charles Schwab fell more than 5%, Expedia about 4%, and Amazon blocked in-site shopping. The market is trading both “agents lift token/storage consumption” and “intermediary platforms get bypassed.”
🎯 Beneficiaries: META, MU, AMD ; Key catalyst: Real agent usage versus platform bans, which will decide whether compute demand actually converts.
3. SOX streak continues; power and high-speed interconnect catch up
The Nasdaq closed at 27,244.28, another record close; SOX rose 2.06%. Monolithic Power ( MPWR ) gained more than 8% to lead the Nasdaq 100, Astera Labs more than 6%, with ARM , Intel , and TSMC ADRs also higher. The move is still spreading after AMD first crossed a $1 trillion market cap on Monday. Capital is rotating from GPU leaders into power management, interconnect, and CPU alternatives.
🎯 Beneficiaries: MPWR, ALAB , AMD, INTC ; Key catalyst: AI server power and bandwidth bottlenecks; watch whether volume can keep up with index highs.
4. NVIDIA puts agentic capability into open-source robotics
At ROSCon in Toronto, NVIDIA released Isaac ROS 5.0, adding agentic workflows for about 1.3 million ROS developers, with support for ROS Lyrical / Ubuntu 24.04. FoundationPose object-pose tracking is up to about 5.5x faster, and reusable pick-and-place skills are included. Coverage runs from Jetson Orin Nano to Thor; Intrinsic, Flexiv, and Universal Robots are already integrated. Physical AI is moving from demos to a deployable toolchain.
🎯 Beneficiaries: NVDA , TSLA ; Key catalyst: ROSCon launch and Jetson Thor shipment expectations; watch whether robotics-theme volume can expand again.
5. Trump–Xi visit starts today: AI dialogue and chip exports in parallel
Xi’s US window is September 23–25, with a White House dinner on the 24th; Jensen Huang, Tim Cook, and Sam Altman are expected to attend. Treasury Secretary Bessent has proposed a US–China AI dialogue and a national-security incident notification mechanism. H200 licenses for China were previously issued, but Chinese customs is still blocking shipments; summit language could instantly reset export expectations.
🎯 Beneficiaries: NVDA, TSM , BABA ; Key catalyst: Summit communiqué, H200 clearance or continued blockage, and whether a formal AI dialogue is stood up.
6. Quantum after-hours spike: IONQ Korea deployment + error-correction breakthrough
IonQ announced a multi-year partnership with South Korea’s SDT to deploy Superion 256 and silicon-vacancy quantum memory, with a packaging and systems-integration plant planned in Gumi. The same day it showed an end-to-end real-time quantum error decoder. The stock finished the regular session nearly flat, then rose about 12% after hours. Quantum World Congress opens September 23, opening a theme-trading window.
🎯 Beneficiaries: IONQ, RGTI , QBTS ; Key catalyst: Conference agenda and Korea hardware-order details; volatility far outruns fundamental verification.
Trading note: Flows have clearly rotated from broad tech into memory, power, interconnect, and physical AI. The Nasdaq is at highs while financials and intermediary software are being de-rated on the Muse narrative. From tonight, watch Trump–Xi comments and oil ; memory is already crowded ahead of MU earnings, so manage pullback risk.
US stocks have been more volatile recently. The above is for information only and does not constitute investment advice.
